Title: OGX Group FY26 earnings jump 51pct on stronger IT infrastructure demand
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: OGX Group Bhd posted a net profit of RM3.76 million on revenue of RM58.3 million for the fourth quarter ended June 30, 2026, driven by continued growth in its information technology (IT) infrastructure solutions business.
There were no year-on-year comparisons for the quarter as the results marked the company's third interim financial report since its ACE Market listing in March.
For the full financial year (FY26), net profit rose 51 per cent to RM23 million from RM15.3 million a year earlier, while revenue jumped 61 per cent to RM284.7 million from RM176 million.
The group said revenue from its IT infrastructure solutions segment reached RM220 million during the year, supported by the completion of more projects.
Executive director and managing director Tan Suan Loong said FY26 marked the group's strongest financial performance to date, driven by sustained demand for its IT infrastructure solutions and the successful execution of its growth strategies.
"These results reflect the strength of our business fundamentals and reinforce our confidence in the group's long-term growth prospects.
"As we move forward, we remain focused on expanding our capabilities, strengthening our market position and delivering sustainable value to our shareholders," he said in a statement,
Tan said the company remains optimistic about its long-term growth prospects, supported by continued investments in digital infrastructure and rising demand for enterprise networking, data centre and cybersecurity solutions.
He said OGX's recent appointment as Nokia's authorised distributor in Malaysia has strengthened its enterprise networking capabilities, enabling the company to better support increasingly complex enterprise data centre projects.
"As part of our growth strategy, we are also progressing towards the launch of our Security Operations Centre (SOC), which will enhance our cybersecurity capabilities and complement our end-to-end IT infrastructure solutions.
"These initiatives will strengthen our capabilities and position OGX for its next phase of growth," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bursa slips ahead of Fed meeting, tech earnings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed marginally lower on Tuesday as investors turned cautious ahead of a busy week featuring the US Federal Reserve's (Fed) policy meeting and earnings releases from major US technology companies.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) slid 0.61 of a point or 0.04 per cent to 1,712.48 from yesterday's close of 1,713.09.
The benchmark index, which opened 1.14 points weaker at 1,711.95, moved between 1,703.83 and 1,715.02 during the day's trading.
In the broader market, decliners outstripped gainers 717 to 348, while 536 counters were unchanged, 1,179 untraded, and 36 suspended.
Turnover rose to 2.94 billion units valued at RM2.56 billion from 2.86 billion units valued at RM2.24 billion on Monday.
IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said trading activity was subdued as market participants awaited greater clarity on the Fed's interest rate outlook and whether second quarter earnings from the technology sector can sustain the global artificial intelligence (AI)-driven rally.
Among companies in the tech sector are Meta Platforms Inc, Microsoft Corporation, Amazon.com Inc and Apple Inc.
"Despite Brent crude oil prices falling more than two per cent, reflecting easing geopolitical concerns and improved supply expectations, it failed to lift market sentiment as investors preferred to remain on the sidelines," he told Bernama.
Meanwhile, Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said there was subdued buying interest today in line with weaker regional markets as investors reassessed the outlook for AI investments.
"Concerns intensified after reports that Nvidia's AI financing commitments had reportedly exceeded US$750 billion, raising questions whether AI demand can keep pace with the industry's aggressive spending plans.
"The news triggered a broad sell-off in global semiconductor stocks, weighing on overall market sentiment across the region," he said.
Among the heavyweights, CIMB fell four sen to RM7.76, while Public Bank rose one sen to RM5.19, Tenaga Nasional gained 20 sen to RM14.66, and Maybank as well as IHH Healthcare remained flat at RM10.90 and RM8.34, respectively.
As for the active stocks, VS Industry slipped one sen to 22 sen, SNS Network Technology and Dagang Nexchange lost two sen each to 54 sen and 43 sen respectively, Tanco added 1.5 sen to 26 sen, and Zentrix AI inched up half a sen to 69 sen.
Among the top gainers, Nestle firmed RM2.36 to RM93.66, Ideal Capital jumped 25 sen to RM4, KLCC Property and REITS surged 15 sen to RM8.84, Hong Leong Bank climbed 20 sen to RM22.30, and Dutch Lady Milk Industries added 18 sen to RM32.
Malaysian Pacific Industries led the top losers list, falling RM2.06 to RM44, while UMS Integration dropped 68 sen to RM7.22, Fraser & Neave lost 34 sen to RM27.50, Kelington sank 31 sen to RM7.90, and Allianz slumped 30 sen to RM21.00.

Title: Zahid: BN staying grounded despite predictions of Negri Sembilan win
Article:
SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional (BN) remains grounded despite predictions that it could secure victory in the Negri Sembilan election on Aug 1, with the coalition refusing to become overconfident.
Its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said BN would continue to position itself as the "underdog" to ensure its machinery and leaders remained vigilant throughout the campaign.
"We are indeed the underdog in this state election, and we do not want to create the impression that we are overly confident.
"We are only confident in what we are doing. We believe we can offer voters and the people of Negri Sembilan something different from what they are receiving now," he told reporters after officiating the Central Zone Rubber Industry Smallholders Development Authority (Risda) Convention today.
Zahid, who is also the rural and regional development minister was responding to an analysis by former Bangi member of parliament Dr Ong Kian Ming, who predicted that BN could win up to 25 seats in the election.
He said maintaining an underdog mindset was crucial to ensuring the party leadership and election machinery did not overlook any group of voters or make statements that could offend the public.
"This underdog approach is important to remind our leaders and party machinery not to do anything out of the ordinary or make statements that voters would find unacceptable.
"That is why we are working with humility and appealing to the people of Negri Sembilan to give BN another opportunity to transform the state," he said.
Zahid said the advantage generally lies with the incumbent coalition, making it necessary for BN to work harder to regain public confidence.
"Through our manifesto, BN is committed to creating 50,000 new jobs in the state over the next five years. We will also focus on technical and vocational education and training to enable the workforce to earn premium wages," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ramanan: Locals first when hiring, foreign workers only when needed
Article:
SEREMBAN: Malaysians must be given priority for available job opportunities before employers consider hiring foreign workers, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said.
He said the policy was aligned with the Human Resources Ministry's primary objective of ensuring employment opportunities were offered to local workers first.
"As the Human Resources Minister, my foremost priority is jobs for Malaysians. Job offers must always go to locals first. If there are no takers, then yes, we can offer them to foreigners, provided the recruitment complies with Malaysia's laws and regulations," he told reporters when asked to comment on a proposal to allow legally recognised Rohingya refugees in Malaysia to take up employment.
Ramanan was speaking after his official visit to the Indian Community Socio-Economic Development Programme (PPSMI) at SJKT Ladang Senawang here today.
He said the ministry would streamline the application process for foreign workers, particularly in the services sector, in line with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's directive to expedite the recruitment of foreign labour where required.
Ramanan said he had instructed all relevant departments under the ministry to reduce unnecessary bureaucracy and avoid delays in processing applications.
"The Prime Minister has given us 30 days to resolve the matter, but I intend to expedite the process. I hope we can complete it within 20 days, subject to issues involving human resources, security screening and related procedures," he said.
Last Friday, Anwar instructed the ministry and relevant agencies to resolve applications for foreign worker recruitment, particularly in the restaurant sector, within one month.
The Prime Minister said the government recognised the urgent need for restaurant operators to address labour shortages while ensuring the recruitment of foreign workers remained properly regulated.
Malaysia currently caps the number of foreign workers allowed in the labour market.
Under the 12th Malaysia Plan (12MP), foreign workers must not account for more than 15 per cent of the national workforce, while the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) aims to reduce the proportion to 10 per cent by 2030.
–Bernama
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 113 refugees relocated after overnight police screening
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: All 113 Rohingya refugees who gathered outside the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) office in Jalan Bukit Petaling have been relocated after undergoing overnight police screening and identity verification.
The refugees, who had travelled from Kampung Kuala Muda, Penang, were taken to the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters in police trucks on Monday night.
Their relocation yesterday, after the screening process, was coordinated by several non-governmental organisations (NGOs).
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said checks during the documentation and identity verification process found that all 113 individuals possessed valid UNHCR documents.
Meanwhile, UNHCR said it had worked closely with authorities after the group was brought to the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters to see to their needs.
"UNHCR engaged the relevant authorities to support documentation verification, ensure that immediate protection and needs were addressed, and identify appropriate solutions.
"These efforts contributed to their transfer to alternative accommodation, which is ongoing," the agency said.
The group had travelled to Kuala Lumpur after being evicted from their settlement in Kampung Kuala Muda, Kedah, following weeks of mediation involving local authorities, government agencies, UNHCR and other stakeholders that failed to secure alternative accommodation.
Earlier, Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the 113 individuals could not be placed in the department's detention depots, which are reserved for foreigners without valid travel or legal documents.
Zakaria said refugees holding UNHCR cards were allowed to remain in the country on humanitarian grounds, but stressed that authorities would not compromise on any breaches of Malaysian laws.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 17-year-old boy drowns after being swept away in Sungai Kampar
Article:
GOPENG: A 17-year-old boy drowned after he was swept away while swimming in Sungai Kampar near Kebun Pak Wan here today.
The victim was identified as Amirul Danish Afizal.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received an emergency call about 1.45pm before personnel from the Gopeng Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the location.
He said the victim was found within 10 minutes after firefighters and members of the Fire and Rescue Academy of Malaysia (FRAM) Tronoh, who were conducting training nearby, launched a search operation.
"FRAM personnel immediately carried out a surface search at the location where the victim was reported missing.
"The victim was found about 15 to 20 metres from the spot where he was last seen jumping into the river," he said.
He said after the victim was retrieved from the river, firefighters and FRAM personnel provided initial treatment and performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) continuously for about an hour while waiting for medical assistance.
"Medical officers from the Health Ministry later examined the victim and confirmed that he had died at the scene.
"The body of the victim was then handed over to the police," he said, adding that the operation ended at 4.18pm
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid sees 88 per cent early voting turnout as positive sign
Article:
SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi described the over 88 per cent early voting turnout as a positive sign ahead of polling day on Aug 1.
He said the high turnout reflected strong democratic participation and hoped the momentum would continue until polling day.
"I congratulate the early voters because the Election Commission (EC) has informed us that the turnout was very high, exceeding 88 per cent.
"If this can be sustained on polling day this Saturday, it will be a very encouraging trend," he told reporters after officiating the Central Zone Rubber Industry Smallholders Development Authority (Risda) convention today.
Zahid who is also the rural and regional development minister however said that BN remained humble and continued to regard itself as the underdog in the Negri Sembilan state election.
"With only three days left before polling, I have instructed our election machinery to continue engaging with voters and addressing any issues they may face on polling day.
"We hope our machinery will remain steadfast in carrying out their duties. I also thank our colleagues from divisions across the country and other states who have come forward to assist the local election machinery.
"Hopefully, this coordinated effort will continue until 6pm on Aug 1," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: France police find five dead babies in a home
Article:
MARSEILLE: French police have found the bodies of five babies in cardboard boxes at the home of a couple in southeast France, several sources said on Tuesday.
Police made the discovery in the town of Orange after the woman gave birth to a healthy baby on Monday, sources close to the investigation said, without providing details.
In March, a French court jailed a 44-year-old woman for 25 years over the deaths of two of her newborn babies, who police found in the family freezer.
In 2018, a court sentenced a woman with a depressive and sometimes violent husband to eight years in prison for drowning five of her newborn babies and freezing their bodies.
In 2015, another court jailed a mother for nine years for killing eight of her newborns, with the jury finding she had impaired judgement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haunted house guide jailed for sexually assaulting 13-year-old girl
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A haunted house guide at a theme park was today sentenced to three years' jail by the Sessions Court after pleading guilty to sexually assaulting a 13-year-old girl.
The court heard that Md Israful Alam, 30, a Bangladeshi, had touched the girl while she was queueing inside the haunted house at a theme park in a shopping mall.
The offence happened about 12.30pm on Feb 7.
Shocked, the girl told her mother, who lodged a police report.
The accused was arrested the same day.
Closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showed the accused committing the offence while standing behind the victim.
He was charged under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act, which provides for a maximum jail sentence of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
Sessions Court judge Datin Surita Budin ordered Israful to serve his sentence from the date of his arrest on Feb 7 and to undergo counselling while in prison.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Shakila Mohd Shariff urged the court to impose a deterrent sentence, saying it would send a clear message that sexual offences against children would not be tolerated.
"The victim was a cheerful girl who enjoyed recreational activities with her family.
"However, because of the accused's actions at a place meant for recreation, she is now afraid to go out and remains traumatised.
"The trauma has been prolonged and continues to affect her to this day," she said.
In mitigation, defence counsel Kelvin Sidhu pleaded for a lighter sentence, citing his client's early guilty plea and the fact that he supports his wife and seven-year-old child.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Neutrality key to keeping Malaysia attractive to investors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: As geopolitical tensions continue to redraw the global investment map, Malaysia must remain firmly neutral to preserve its appeal as a trusted destination for foreign investors, investment and central bank leaders said.
Malaysian Investment Development Authority chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz said taking sides in an increasingly fragmented world could undermine Malaysia's ability to attract investments on its own merits.
"One must not underestimate the importance of geopolitics," he said during a panel discussion at Bank Negara Malaysia's Sasana Symposium 2026.
"That's why I believe it is important that the government continues to play that position where Malaysia continues to be neutral in its approach."
Bank Negara Malaysia deputy governor Datuk Marzunisham Omar echoed the view, saying businesses are no longer chasing the lowest costs alone.
Instead, they are looking for resilient economies capable of weathering geopolitical tensions, export restrictions and growing geoeconomic fragmentation.
He said Malaysia's neutral stance has enabled it to diversify both its trade relationships and sources of foreign direct investment, strengthening its position as an attractive investment destination.
"Businesses are looking for resilience, not only cost, knowing that this is the environment that we will be operating in, which is the environment of geopolitical tensions, geoeconomic limitations, export restrictions and so on.
"I do agree with Tengku Zafrul that we should maintain our neutrality because we have benefited from this. Our trade is very diversified. Similarly, the source of our foreign direct investment is also highly diversified.
"So that goes to show that our position as the indispensable connector has benefited us and we should continue with an open trade and investment policy," he said.
Marzunisham said neutrality alone would not be enough if Malaysia failed to provide a stable economic environment.
He said investors also look for macroeconomic stability, low inflation, a stable exchange rate and predictable government policies before committing long-term capital.
"There is a need to always maintain macroeconomic stability, price stability, low inflation and a stable exchange rate. These are very important preconditions to provide a conducive environment for trade, investment and business decisions to be made, for businesses to thrive," he said.
Marzunisham added that Bank Negara would continue to maintain an open and liberal foreign exchange policy to facilitate trade and investment flows.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asean ministers voice concern over Middle East tensions, online scams
Article:
JAKARTA: Asean foreign ministers expressed concern over escalating tensions in the Middle East and the growing threat posed by transnational online scams, calling for stronger regional cooperation, Asean Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn said on Tuesday, reported Xinhua.
Speaking at the Asean Secretariat in South Jakarta, Kao said the ministers discussed geopolitical rivalry, regional security and developments in the Middle East during their annual retreat in Manila.
The ministers later issued a joint statement calling for dialogue, expressing concern over the humanitarian situation in Gaza and reaffirming the need to protect civilians in accordance with international law.
Kao said the ministers also agreed to strengthen coordination through Asean-led security mechanisms to mitigate the impact of the conflict on Southeast Asia, particularly on energy and food security, supply chains and the safety of Asean nationals in the region.
The ministers also identified online scams and transnational organised crime as pressing regional challenges, warning that increasingly sophisticated criminal networks are fuelling human trafficking, money laundering and the misuse of digital technologies across borders.
"This is an issue that is affecting all of us now, and there is a need to strengthen regional cooperation, both within Asean and between Asean and its external partners," Kao said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Labourer gets six years' jail for robbery and sexual assault of foreign woman
Article:
BESUT: A 29-year-old labourer was sentenced to a total of six years in prison and one stroke of the rotan by the Sessions Court and magistrate's court here today after pleading guilty to robbing and sexually assaulting a foreign woman.
Muhammad Ayub Firdaus Mohd Nor pleaded guilty to the charges after they were read out separately before Sessions Court judge Ahmad Fadhli Mahmud and magistrate Nurliyana Md Zukri.
In the Sessions Court, the charge stated that Ayub robbed the foreigner by forcibly taking her personal belongings during an incident that took place in a bushy area near Bukit Bubus about 1.30pm on July 25.
The charge was framed under Section 392 of the Penal Code for robbery.
Upon hearing the plea, Ahmad Fadhli handed down the sentence for the first charge.
"The court sentences the accused to four years' jail and one stroke of the rotan for the offence of robbery," he said.
Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Akmal Mohd Jazlee prosecuted.
In a separate proceeding at the magistrate's court, Ayub also pleaded guilty to using criminal force against the same woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.
He was charged with committing the second offence at the same location and time as the robbery under Section 354 of the Penal Code.
Nurliyana sentenced Ayub to an additional two years in prison.
Deputy public prosecutor Nurul Najah Azhar prosecuted in the second case.
With the conclusion of both proceedings, Ayub faces a total of six years in prison and one stroke of the rotan for the attack on the foreigner.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: What are 'fire clouds', the ominous phenomenon seen in France?
Article:
FIREFIGHTERS battling devastating fires in France have had to contend with a new threat: immense fire clouds that create their own wind and even lightning that can spark fresh blazes.
Known as "fire clouds" or pyrocumulonimbus clouds, these ominous-looking thunderstorms are created by extreme wildfires and can exacerbate already extremely dangerous conditions.
This phenomenon, which is new to France, is yet another consequence of human-caused climate change, according to French researcher Jean-Baptiste Filippi, who studies wildfires.
As firefighters in southwest France struggle to bring a forest inferno under control before yet another heatwave descends on the country, Filippi told AFP about the phenomenon.
What is a fire cloud?
It is a storm where a column of air forms above a fire.
It starts off as a cute little white cloud – a cumulus cloud, which is formed because water vapour has turned into tiny droplets.
As the Sun heats the ground, the water vapour suddenly condenses. The cumulus becomes a much larger cloud, containing thousands of tonnes of suspended water.
Then, when the surrounding air has become heated enough, it forms a column with an anvil-shaped cloud – the cumulonimbus.
This condenses even more air and generates more energy, with updrafts of more than 150 kilometres an hour.
It then rains, but the rain evaporates before it reaches the ground.
But it still cools the atmosphere where it falls, creating strong downdrafts.
Are fire clouds rare?
It is a common phenomenon in Portugal, California and Australia, where firefighters are more used to them. In Portugal, they had been rare until the deadly 2017 fires in Pedrogao Grande changed things.
In France, pyrocumulonimbus clouds are quite new. There were some in Landiras south of Bordeaux in 2022, but not for long.
Therefore, we need to learn how to manage fires that creates their own wind – this is something relatively new.
Is climate change to blame?
Yes, it is. A consequence of global warming is more frequent heatwaves. While thunderstorms are common in the region of this fire, thunderstorm conditions after three successive heatwaves is a new combination.
Are they predictable?
Weather services can predict thunderstorms. But because these storms are located directly above a fire, we would need to know the fire's exact location in advance. That's impossible.
We can predict the conditions that will lead to these fires, but we won't know exactly where they are.
The biggest challenge is how unpredictable they are. The fire in France's southwest Gironde region started with northerly winds, then westerly, then southerly, then easterly, then back again to the south, then the west...
On top of that, there is this potential energy in the atmosphere which meant that, locally, the convection column sucked up the embers and carried the fire further afield.
The local conditions became catastrophic and the rate of the fire's spread was staggering.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Missing KK teen found safe in Inanam
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A 13-year-old student reported missing after leaving the grounds of SMK Lok Yuk in Likas on Monday has been found safe in Inanam.
A family member, who declined to be identified, shared the update on social media.
The girl was under police care to assist in investigations into her disappearance before being reunited with her family.
The family expressed gratitude to the police and the public for their concern and assistance in sharing information that led to the student's safe recovery.
They have yet to disclose the circumstances surrounding
her disappearance.
Earlier, the Kota Kinabalu district police headquarters issued a statement on its official Facebook page regarding the girl's disappearance after she was dropped off in front other school at about 5.55am yesterday.
Checks later revealed that she had not attended school, prompting her family to lodge a missing person's report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Contractor: No RM1mil Bersatu donation without Jana Wibawa project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A contractor told the High Court that his company would not have donated RM1 million to Bersatu if it had not been awarded a RM141 million Jana Wibawa project.
Nepturis Sdn Bhd founder Lian Tan Chuan testified that the award followed what he described as support from then prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin for the company's application to build the North Klang district police headquarters.
"If Nepturis had not been awarded the IPD Klang Utara project, I would not have made any contribution to Bersatu. This was the first time Nepturis made a political donation," he said in his witness statement.
Lian was testifying as the 19th prosecution witness in the corruption and money laundering trial involving Muhyiddin before judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin here today.
The businessman told the court that during the Covid-19 pandemic, he sought government projects and was introduced by businessman Datuk Azman Yusoff to the Jana Wibawa programme.
According to Lian, Azman informed him that companies seeking projects under the programme required Muhyiddin's support as prime minister before introducing him to
Adam Radlan, who allegedly claimed to have close ties with Muhyiddin.
Lian said Adam instructed him to prepare application letters seeking Muhyiddin's support for the IPD Klang Utara project.
Besides Nepturis, he also submitted four similar letters under the names of other companies before handing all five documents to Adam at Publika in early February 2021.
A few days later, Adam allegedly told him that Muhyiddin had minuted his support on the applications, giving Lian confidence that Nepturis stood a strong chance of securing the project.
Lian said such an endorsement carried significant weight in government procurement.
He said Azman later told him that Nepturis had a strong chance of securing the project and asked him to contribute RM1 million directly to Bersatu if the company succeeded, as Adam had obtained Muhyiddin's support.
Lian said he agreed to the request and also appointed Azman's company, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, as Nepturis' business development consultant under a six-month agreement worth RM1 million to assist with tender preparation, technical specifications and supplier pricing.
The witness said Nepturis was awarded the RM141 million contract on Jan 12, 2022.
After informing Azman and Adam of the successful bid, he said Azman reminded him of their earlier agreement to contribute RM1 million to Bersatu.
Lian maintained that the donation was made following Azman's request and that he believed Muhyiddin's support had enabled Nepturis to secure the project.
Muhyiddin, 79, is facing four charges of abusing his position to obtain RM232.5 million in gratification for Bersatu in connection with the Jana Wibawa programme, as well as three charges of laundering RM200 million. He has pleaded not guilty to all seven charges.
The trial continues.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Major quake in southern Japan knocks out power, disrupts transport
Article:
TOKYO: An earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.1 struck Japan's southern Kumamoto prefecture on Tuesday, knocking out power to thousands of homes, snarling travel and triggering evacuation orders and warnings for aftershocks.
Speaking to reporters at her office in Tokyo, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said the extent of casualties and property damage was being assessed.
"We have already been informed that people have been injured," Takaichi said.
"Power outages and fires have occurred in some areas, and there has also been damage to roads and bridges and the collapse of buildings.
"Above all, I ask everyone to take action to protect themselves, including evacuating to a safe location."
Public broadcaster NHK showed several buildings on fire or collapsed, large cracks along roads, including an elevated highway, and a derailed goods train.
More than 150,000 people were instructed to go to evacuation centres, the disaster management agency said.
TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, evacuated workers from its plant in the area as a precaution, a spokesperson for the firm said.
A spokesperson for electronics firm Sony, which also has a plant there, said it was checking the situation.
Residents in the areas that felt the biggest tremors must beware of further strong quakes for about a week as well as the risk of landslides, an official for the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) said.
[[nid:1499010]]
The Japanese government issued emergency earthquake warnings for Kumamoto, Nagasaki, Kagoshima, Fukuoka, Saga, Oita, and Miyazaki prefectures, all on Japan's southern Kyushu island.
The JMA also initially issued a tsunami warning for a wave measuring one metre but later lifted it.
Japan is one of the world's most earthquake-prone countries, with a tremor occurring at least every five minutes.
Located along the "Ring of Fire" of volcanoes and oceanic trenches partly encircling the Pacific Basin, Japan accounts for about 20 per cent of the world's earthquakes of magnitude 6.0 or more.
Kyushu Electric Power said about 40,000 homes had lost power as a result of the latest quake, while railway company JR Kyushu said that it had suspended services, including its high-speed bullet trains.
Kumamoto airport also shut its runway, as airlines diverted and cancelled flights.
Telecoms operators KDDI and Docomo said there was disruption to their mobile phone services due to power shortages and transmission-line failures.
There were no irregularities reported at the nuclear power stations in the area, Japan's nuclear regulation authority said.
A massive earthquake in Kumamoto 10 years ago killed 275 people and injured a further 2,739, according to an official count, and damaged thousands of buildings including the city's castle, a top tourist site.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan polls: Johari urges Malay leaders to reject racial political narratives
Article:
JEMPOL: Malay leaders must not be trapped by racial political narratives but instead must take responsibility for safeguarding the interests of all communities in the country, said Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
He said Malaysia was built as a multiracial nation, with Malays forming the majority population.
He added that leadership must therefore be inclusive and provide equal treatment, rather than divide the people based on racial differences.
"I do not know in what context any individual was speaking (about race), but Malaysia is a country with a multiracial society, with Malays forming the majority.
"If we want to be leaders in this country as Malays and Bumiputera, we must be responsible for looking after all communities, including minorities," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after meeting the Barisan Nasional election machinery at the Palong 3 Felda settlement here today.
Also present was BN candidate for Palong Datuk Mustapha Nagoor.
On narratives that segregate society along racial lines during election campaigns, Johari stressed that such an approach would not benefit the country.
Although Umno is a Malay-based party, he said BN has remained a multiracial coalition representing Malaysian society since its formation.
"Umno is a Malay party, but when we contest elections, we use the BN platform, which represents all races and religions in the country.
"For more than 60 years of governing the country, BN has never contested under the Umno name alone because its spirit has always been based on cooperation among various communities," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bar warns Admiralty Jurisdiction Bill falls short of global standards
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Bar has voiced its disappointment over the newly introduced Admiralty Jurisdiction Bill 2026, saying the proposed legislation falls short of international benchmarks.
The Bar also said it could undermine the nation's ambition to become a leading regional maritime hub.
Bar president Anand Raj said the draft legislation failed to meaningfully incorporate recommendations developed through years of extensive stakeholder consultations.
He said the proposed legislation in its present form could leave the maritime sector worse off than under the current law.
"Any departure from internationally recognised admiralty principles may lead to uncertainty in certain aspects of
maritime disputes and may diminish the competitiveness of Malaysia
as a preferred maritime legal hub within the region," he said in a statement.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said had said on July 13 that the bill would be referred to a special select committee for further scrutiny before being debated in the Dewan Rakyat.
She had proposed setting up a 12-member team to comb through the legislation.
Azalina had said the committee would examine the bill's scope, structure and drafting, with a view to proposing amendments.
It would also prepare a statement containing its views and recommendations, or propose a new bill, within three months.
Anand said the Bar had previously proposed a modern, stand-alone admiralty framework drawn from internationally recognised benchmarks, including the United Kingdom's Senior Courts Act 1981 and the 1952 and 1999 international conventions on arrest of ships.
He said aligning with global standards was essential to providing legal certainty and predictability for shipowners, seafarers, charterers, cargo interests, financiers and insurers operating in Malaysian waters.
"The Malaysian Bar welcomed the decision by the Dewan Rakyat to refer the bill for further scrutiny.
"We also urged the committee to engage constructively with industry experts and give serious consideration to the Bar's recommendations before returning the bill to the House.
"It is unfathomable that the 2026 bill should be subject to politicisation or partisan politics."
He added that Malaysia possessed all the necessary attributes to emerge as a premier venue for maritime dispute resolution.

Title: Massachusetts mother goes on trial for killing her three children
Article:
DUXBURY: A Massachusetts jury heard dueling accounts on Monday for why a mother killed her three young children in 2023, a tragedy that a defense lawyer said was due to her suffering from postpartum mental illness and that a prosecutor called a planned murder.
Lindsay Clancy admits that she strangled her three children in January 2023 with exercise bands in the basement of her home in the Boston suburb of Duxbury.
She then cut herself with a knife and jumped from a second-story window in a failed attempt to end her own life that left her paralysed.
During his opening statement in Plymouth County Superior Court, defence attorney Kevin Reddington told jurors that Clancy, now 35, had struggled for months with postpartum mental health issues following the birth of her third child.
"This is a woman that was suffering from psychosis at the time that she went down to that basement," Reddington said.
He portrayed her as a loving mother who was plagued with suicidal thoughts and postpartum mental health issues before the killings, leading her to repeatedly seek treatment from multiple healthcare providers who had prescribed her a myriad of drugs that did not help.
"She's living her own hell," he said. "She knows what happened with those kids."
Assistant District Attorney Shanan Buckingham did not dispute that Clancy, a former labor and delivery nurse at Massachusetts General Hospital, had been dealing with mental health issues before she killed her children, Cora, 5; Dawson, 3; and 8-month-old Callan.
But Buckingham said, "This is not a public debate about women's mental health and how the medical system treats women," and that instead the case turned on the question of whether Clancy appreciated the wrongfulness of killing her children but chose to do so anyway.
[[nid:1498997]]
She said the evidence showed Clancy sent her husband at the time, Patrick, out to pick up a food order after mapping on her phone the time it would take for him to return home so she could work "swiftly to accomplish a very specific goal: to kill."
Called as the trial's first witness, Patrick Clancy, who is now divorced from Lindsay, said his wife had been discharged from a psychiatric hospital less than two weeks earlier but showed no signs she planned to hurt herself or her kids in the days that followed.
She had a "normal" demeanour when he left to pick up dinner.
"I came upstairs," he said. "I took Callan for a minute, and I rocked him by my knees, kissed Cora on the head, and I said I'll be right back."
The trial ended for the day before he could speak about what happened upon his return.
Buckingham had told jurors that when Patrick got back, he discovered his wife in the backyard.
He called 911, and after first responders arrived, Patrick Clancy found the children in the basement and screamed that they had been killed, she said.
"This was a woman who no longer liked the life she thought she wanted; it was getting harder and harder to control," she said.
"And when she saw the opportunity to escape, she made the selfish choice to take it and to take Cora, Dawson, and Callan first before attempting to take her own life."
Clancy faces a mandatory sentence of life in prison if she is convicted on any of the first-degree murder charges she faces. The trial is expected to last six to eight weeks.

Title: World risks HIV resurgence as funding falls 18 per cent: UNAIDS
Article:
GENEVA: The world risks a resurgence of the HIV epidemic after global funding fell by nearly a fifth last year, the UN body fighting AIDS said on Monday.
Washington previously accounted for 75 per cent of international HIV funding before President Donald Trump's return to the White House in January 2025.
That month he ordered a temporary halt to all HIV-related funding before restoring life-saving HIV work days later, although most prevention efforts were curtailed.
"The international community has entered a period of profound political and financial upheaval that threatens decades of hard-won gains against HIV," UNAIDS said in its 60-page report released at the start of an International AIDS conference in Brazil.
"Without renewed commitment and action, the world risks a resurgence of the HIV epidemic."
Funding fell by 18 per cent to US$7.3 billion in 2025, which was the lowest level in nearly two decades, the report said.
That risks reversing progress that has driven down new HIV infections and AIDS-related deaths to their lowest level in more than 30 years, it said.
"The current fragility of the HIV response puts these gains at risk unless global solidarity is restored and inequalities are addressed."
The report also repeated that the global goal to end AIDS by 2030 was off track, saying that reduced funding as well as other crises like Ebola were hampering efforts. Some 1.2 million people caught HIV last year.
The impact of foreign funding cuts for HIV was partially offset, however, by increases in domestic spending.
That meant an overall decline of six per cent in total HIV resources last year, the UNAIDS report said.
But not all governments were able to step in. Some of the biggest declines in spending on prevention programmes were in sub-Saharan Africa, which accounts for about half of new global infections.
National data for Cameroon, Nigeria and Zambia showed more than a 50 per cent decline in the number of people receiving pre-exposure ‌prophylaxis, or PrEP.
"HIV funding disruptions severely impacted HIV prevention, testing and key components of treatment programmes, such as the range of community-led services that reach the people most affected by HIV," the report said.

Title: Azalina: Local candidates better placed to address community issues
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Local candidates are better placed to understand and address community issues, making them the ideal choice in the Negri Sembilan elections, said Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
Azalina said state assembly representatives should be easily accessible to constituents, noting that state-level responsibilities differed from those of members of parliament as they focused more on local concerns.
"We want candidates who can provide service to the people, especially local candidates who live here.
"A state assembly is different from Parliament because it is more focused on local issues and problems.
"When the candidate is from the area, they have a deeper understanding of the community and can always be present for the people," she said.
She said BN's candidate for the constituency would secure a convincing victory, citing encouraging feedback received during engagements with voters.
On BN's strategy to engage young voters, she said the coalition had long prioritised youth outreach through Umno Youth and Puteri Umno, well before the implementation of the Undi18 initiative.
"This is not something new for us. BN and Umno have been preparing for this for a long time. We did not only start reaching out to young voters after Undi18.
"Many young voters come from families that have long supported BN, so communication within families and communities remains very important," she said.
Commenting on BN's manifesto for the Negri Sembilan election, Azalina said its main strength was consistency, reflecting the coalition's extensive experience in governance and elections.

Title: Government allocates RM1.7 billion to replace ageing water pipes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The federal government has approved an allocation of RM1.7 billion under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) to replace about 1,800km of critical water pipes nationwide between 2026 and 2030.
Deputy Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Rahman Mohamad said the programme would prioritise the replacement of ageing asbestos-cement (AC) pipes and other critical pipelines that have exceeded their design lifespan to reduce the country's Non-Revenue Water (NRW) rate.
"Through the implementation of this programme, the government is committed to strengthening the resilience of the national water supply system through the phased renewal of ageing assets, reducing NRW rates and ensuring all replacement works are carried out in accordance with stringent safety standards for the well-being of the people," he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Negara today.
He was responding to a question from Senator Datuk Wu Him Ven on the government's action plan for replacing asbestos-cement water pipes.
On NRW statistics, Abdul Rahman said the rate for Peninsular Malaysia and the Federal Territory of Labuan stood at 34.4 per cent in 2025, while the figure for 2026 would only be finalised after the reporting year ends.
Addressing concerns over occupational safety related to the release of asbestos dust during pipe replacement works, he said all projects must comply with regulations and safety standards set by the Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH).
In response to a supplementary question from Senator Phoong Jin Zhe on pipe replacement initiatives in Sabah, Abdul Rahman said the state had identified 110.4km of critical water pipes requiring urgent replacement, with the works estimated to cost RM99.35 million.
He added that, apart from replacing ageing pipelines, the federal government had also allocated RM558,000 to support efforts to reduce Sabah's Non-Revenue Water (NRW) rate.

Title: 113 Rohingya refugees moved to NGO-designated location from KL police headquarters
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 113 refugees who had been temporarily accommodated at the City police headquarters, here, have been transferred to a location designated by a non-governmental organisation (NGO).
City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the group departed from the police headquarters about 4pm.
"All 113 refugees left the headquarters for a destination designated by the NGO, Kaladan from Ampang.
"The group included refugees aged between one month and 60 years old," he said.
It was previously reported that Fadil had said the refugees were moved to the city police headquarters after gathering outside the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) office in Bukit Petaling following their relocation from a settlement in Penang, pending further action by the UN agency.
Fadil said documentation carried out with the assistance of UNHCR found that all 110 Rohingya refugees possessed valid UNHCR documents.
The group comprised 110 Rohingya refugees, one Iraqi man, one Somali woman and one Indonesian woman married to a Rohingya refugee.

Title: Negri Sembilan police deny claims personnel were bribed to vote
Article:
NILAI: Negri Sembilan police have denied allegations by Parti Wawasan Negara coordinator Badrul Hisham Shaharin, better known as Chegubard, that police personnel were bribed to vote for a particular political party.
State police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said an investigation would be carried out if a police report was lodged over the allegations.
"So far, these are merely allegations against the police, and I have been monitoring the matter since the statement was made.
"If a police report is lodged, we will conduct an investigation. If the report concerns misconduct, namely bribery, we will refer the matter to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission," he told a press conference today.
Yesterday, Chegubard claimed that a group of police personnel had visited the Perikatan Nasional media centre and alleged that they had each been paid between RM300 and RM500 to vote for a particular party.
He also claimed that the personnel alleged they had been pressured to disclose the serial numbers on their ballot papers.
Alzafny said police would remain professional, open and transparent, while upholding the highest standards of integrity throughout the election process.

Title: Family shaken after firecrackers allegedly thrown at Kelantan house
Article:
KOTA BARU: A family of eight, including a three-year-old girl, went through a frightening ordeal after an unknown man allegedly threw lit firecrackers at their house in Kampung Wakaf Tanjung Chepa here yesterday.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Azmir Damiri confirmed that police had received a report on the incident, adding that no suspect had been arrested so far.
The incident occurred at about 1.15am when 30-year-old Nur Shairah Solehah Ahmad Norzaki, a mother of three, had just returned from work.
"I suddenly heard several loud explosions that sounded like gunshots outside the house.
"At first, I thought it was either a shooting or a gas explosion.
"I quickly called my mother and my 19-year-old younger brother before checking the CCTV footage installed around the house," she said when met today.
Nur Shairah claimed the footage showed an unidentified man lighting what appeared to be firecrackers before throwing them towards the house.
[[nid:1498976]]
She said eight family members were inside the house during the incident, including her mother, three siblings and her three children, the youngest aged three.
"Alhamdulillah, all of us were safe. We were shocked because we have never received any threats or had problems with anyone.
"I believe this was an act of mischief or sabotage. I hope the police can identify the person responsible and determine the motive," she said.
Nur Shairah added that six vehicles were parked within the compound during the incident, but none was damaged.
She also claimmed that a witness saw a silver Honda car believed to have been used by the suspect before the incident.
Nur Shairah lodged a police report at the Binjai police station, urging the authorities to conduct a thorough investigation.

Title: Keiko Fujimori set to take office as Peru president
Article:
LIMA: Peru's right-wing president-elect Keiko Fujimori will take office on Tuesday, vowing to tackle the wave of crime sweeping the Andean nation.
Fujimori won the June 7 presidential runoff by fewer than 50,000 votes, after losing the past three runoffs.
The 51-year-old came head-to-head with leftist Roberto Sanchez, with her campaign shadowed by the divisive legacy of her father Alberto Fujimori, who ruled Peru in the 1990s.
Alberto Fujimori was jailed for corruption and crimes against humanity committed during what he considered a fight against terrorism.
"It is a party with deep popular roots that has had a dynamic presence in Peruvian politics, even when it was losing elections, because of its uninterrupted presence in Congress," Jeffrey Radzinsky, director of the political consultancy GFP, said of Fujimori's Fuerza Popular party.
Fujimori campaigned on a hardline security platform as Peru faces its worst security crisis in decades, fueled by the spread of both local and foreign criminal gangs that oversee contract killings and extortion.
She has proposed fighting crime by expelling undocumented people, setting up courts with anonymous judges and making prisoners work for their food.
The president-elect has also vowed to tackle the El Nino climate phenomenon, which meteorologists predict will be the most intense and devastating since 1998.
Fuerza Popular is the largest caucus in Congress, but right-wing groups still fall short of the majority required to push through Fujimori's initiatives.
The inauguration ceremony will be attended by leaders including Argentina's Javier Milei, Chile's Jose Antonio Kast, Bolivia's Rodrigo Paz, Ecuador's Daniel Noboa and Uruguay's Yamandu Orsi.
Fujimori will be the country's ninth president in a decade, succeeding interim leader Jose Maria Balcazar. She will govern until 2031.

Title: Ex-unit trust consultant jailed, fined RM2mil for investment scam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A former unit trust consultant was sentenced to 18 months' jail and fined RM2 million by two Sessions Courts after pleading guilty to cheating two men in a securities investment scam.
Amran Mohd Amin, 59, received an 18-month jail sentence and a RM1 million fine from Sessions Court judge Azrul Darus for one charge. He will face an additional six months' jail if he fails to pay the fine.
For the second charge, Sessions Court judge Ilmami Ahmad imposed the same sentence.
The jail terms will run concurrently from Amran's arrest on Sept 8 last year.
Amran was charged with being directly involved in a fraudulent securities purchase scheme involving units in the Kenanga Shariah Growth Opportunities Fund.
He was accused of making false representations to the two victims about an investment through Kenanga Investors Berhad, which led them to purchase bank drafts amounting to RM130,000 and RM10,000 respectively.
The drafts were intended for investment purposes but were later used to purchase unit trust units in an account linked to Amran.
The offences took place at Kenanga Tower, Jalan Tun Razak, between Dec 2021 and June 27, 2022.
Amran was charged under Section 179(b) of the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007, punishable under Section 182 of the same Act.
The offence carries a maximum jail term of 10 years and a fine of not less than RM1 million.
The prosecution was led by deputy public prosecutor Mageswary Karroppiah, assisted by Securities Commission prosecuting officers Adibah Saiful Bahri and Sharifah Noor Effah.
Amran was represented by lawyer Nor Azri Mohd Arif.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Recognising the majority who protect our communities
Article:
LETTERS:
The recent news of several policemen being detained over an extortion case has understandably drawn public attention and raised questions.
While such misconduct is deeply regrettable and cannot be excused, it is only fair that we view this matter in proper perspective.
The individuals concerned are the exceptions, not the rule. The majority of our policemen carries out their duties with courage and dedication.
Day in and day out, they work to maintain public order, protect our communities, fight criminal activity and keep our streets safe.
Their contributions to upholding the rule of law and ensuring our peace of mind are immense and deserve our full recognition and appreciation.
That said, the wrongdoing of these few "rotten apples" must not be overlooked or taken lightly.
Allegations of extortion — especially when foreign nationals are among the victims — strike at the very heart of public trust in our law enforcement system.
Such actions damage the reputation of the entire force, erode confidence in our institutions and can harm the country's standing in the eyes of the world.
The authorities are right to pursue this matter firmly and without compromise.
Those found guilty must face the full consequences of their actions, to send a clear message that such behaviour will never be tolerated.
At the same time, this is also an opportunity to strengthen checks and balances, and ensure the highest standards of conduct are upheld across the force.
We must never allow the misdeeds of a small minority to overshadow the excellent work done by the many.
By acting decisively against those who break the law, and continuing to support the vast majority of officers who serve us well, we can uphold the integrity of our police force and the trust of the people they serve.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
Chairman
Alliance For A Safe Community
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Family of teen killed in drug-fuelled Teluk Intan crash seeks justice
Article:
IPOH: The family of one of two teenage girls killed in a
crash in Teluk Intan
on Sunday wants the driver involved to face the full force of the law after he tested positive for drugs.
The victim's cousin, Afrina Wardina Syamimi Azlizam, 16, said the parents of Nur Atikah Abdullah hope the driver will be held accountable for the death of their youngest child.

Afrina said the last time she communicated with Nur Atikah was on the victim's birthday on July 18 via WhatsApp.

Title: Migrant worker abuse a national security risk: Analyst
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Abuse of Malaysia's migrant worker recruitment ecosystem should no longer be treated solely as a labour or human trafficking issue, but as a national security concern.
Saying this, security and defence analyst Zaki Salleh said the recruitment of foreign workers far beyond actual industry demand could create risks extending well beyond labour market distortions.
"When there are significantly more migrant workers entering the country than available employment opportunities, the implications extend far beyond illegal employment.
"It creates fertile ground for organised crime, human trafficking syndicates, document fraud, illegal settlements, identity abuse and wider security concerns," he said.
Zaki said both the Malaysian and Bangladesh governments deserve recognition for their efforts to reform the recruitment process through greater transparency and digitalisation.
"The willingness shown by both governments to address long-standing structural weaknesses demonstrates a commitment to protecting not only migrant workers but also the national interests of both countries," he added.
He said one of the key reforms has been the introduction of the Foreign Workers Centralised Management System (FWCMS), which digitalises and integrates the recruitment process from source countries to Malaysia.
"Whenever a manual system involves multiple intermediaries, opportunities for manipulation naturally arise.
"Digitalisation reduces discretionary decision-making, creates audit trails and significantly limits opportunities for profiteering."
According to Zaki, while no digital system alone can eliminate abuse entirely, technology substantially raises the barriers against fraudulent activities.
"The more transparent and automated the recruitment process becomes, the more difficult it is for syndicates to exploit loopholes that previously existed within fragmented manual processes."
He noted that Malaysia should continue strengthening digital governance instead of reverting to fragmented systems.
According to information published by Bestinet, FWCMS today operates as a 15-module integrated platform connecting 15 labour source countries, 232 accredited medical centres, and relevant government agencies into a single digital ecosystem.
The platform, it added, manages the processing of more than two million foreign workers annually.
Bestinet noted that the platform has delivered significant operational improvement. This includes reducing processing times from several months to as little as 48 hours for certain processes, virtually eliminating medical report forgery.
This leads to 100 per cent biometric verification to prevent worker impersonation, reduced documentation errors, 99.5 per cent system availability and full medical compliance for arriving workers.
The company said the system was developed through more than 15 years of private investment without direct cost to Malaysian taxpayers.
On its public platform, FWCMS noted that it supports 140 accredited medical centres, works with more than 3,500 recruitment agencies and has received internationally recognised certifications including ISO 9001, ISO 27001 and CMMI Level 3.
This reflects its emphasis on quality management, cybersecurity and software development standards.
The platform has also received international recognition, including the United Nations World Summit Award in 2017 under the Government and Citizen Engagement category, recognising its innovation in digital governance for migrant worker management.
Zaki said the figures indicated that digital governance can significantly improve transparency and operational efficiency, although continued independent oversight and enforcement remain equally important.
"The lesson is not simply that one system works. The lesson is that structural problems require structural solutions.
"Digital platforms provide transparency, but enforcement agencies must continue acting against those who attempt to circumvent the system."
He added that enforcement should extend beyond Malaysia.
"Human trafficking and recruitment abuses are transnational crimes. They cannot be solved by one country acting alone.
"Authorities in both labour-sending and receiving countries must share intelligence, coordinate investigations and undertake joint enforcement operations."
Those who abuse migrant worker recruitment systems are not simply violating administrative procedures, he said.
They also undermine immigration controls, facilitate human trafficking and potentially compromise national security.
Looking ahead, Zaki said Malaysia should continue expanding digital integration across the entire migrant worker ecosystem while strengthening cross-border enforcement cooperation.
"The objective should be a recruitment ecosystem that is transparent, accountable and secure.
"Every loophole that enables illegal profiteering is ultimately a loophole that can be exploited against the country's security interests."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Businessman: Bumi contractor’s RM1m to Bersatu was ‘reward’ after getting RM141m govt project, tapped Muhyiddin’s golf buddy’s help
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Bumiputera contractor Nepturis Sdn Bhd had given RM1 million to political party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (PPBM) in 2022 as a “reward” after the company was awarded a RM141 million government project, instead of as a “donation”, a businessman told the High Court today.
Businessman Lian Tan Chuan, who said he owns 30 per cent of Nepturis’ shares through a verbal agreement with Nepturis’ current two Bumiputera shareholders, added that he believed that the company would not have won the contract without Muhyiddin’s support.
Lian said he had asked Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad, whom he had heard was close to and frequently played golf with Muhyiddin, to help get Muhyiddin’s written support for Nepturis’ application for the RM141 million project.
Lian, 55, said this as the 21st prosecution witness in Bersatu president and former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s power abuse and money laundering trial.
Today, Lian said Nepturis had on February 1, 2021 applied for the project to build the Klang Utara district police headquarters (IPD), and had on January 12, 2022 won the project, and had on February 16, 2022 issued a RM1 million cheque to Bersatu.
This RM1 million cheque was deposited into Bersatu’s AmBank account on February 21, 2022, based on previous banking evidence shown in this trial.
“If Nepturis Sdn Bhd did not succeed in being awarded this IPD Klang Utara project, I will not make any ‘sumbangan’ (donation) to PPBM. This is the first time Nepturis Sdn Bhd made donations to a political party,” Lian told the High Court.
Lian said the RM1 million was paid to Bersatu upon the request of Malaysia’s Bumiputera contractors’ association president and Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) director Datuk Azman Yusoff.
Lian also voiced his belief that Nepturis had been given the project through the company’s application letter, which he said was supported by Muhyiddin as the PM then and Bersatu president.
“I believe if my company’s application letter was not supported by Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and was not processed by the Prime Minister’s Office, my company would certainly not succeed through the Ministry of Finance’s evaluation process and subsequently succeed in being awarded this project by JKR,” he said.
Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik raised an objection over Lian’s remarks on his belief that the project award to Nepturis was due to Muhyiddin’s support and said this should be left for the court to conclude, with the judge then recording down this objection.
Deputy Public Prosecutor, Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin is pictured at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Complex on March 11, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Was RM1m to Bersatu a ‘donation’ or ‘reward’?
Asked by lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin if he understood what “donation” and “reward” meant, Lian explained that a donation is something given voluntarily “with no strings attached, without getting anything in return” or without asking for anything in return.
“But ‘reward’ is I get something then I reward to that person. That is my definition of ‘reward’ lah,” he said, later also defining a reward as “a kind of token of appreciation for what he or she has done for me”.
When asked by Wan Shaharuddin if Nepturis’ RM1 million to Bersatu was a donation or reward, Lian said: “I think it is a reward.”
Lian said RM1 million is a big sum for Nepturis as it could be used as capital to carry out projects, and that he would not have made the donation to Bersatu if Azman did not ask him to do so.
When asked why he did not pay the RM1 million before the project was awarded, Lian said this was because his agreement with Azman was to make the RM1 million donation to Bersatu after Nepturis gets the project.
While Nepturis had only started receiving payments from the government from April 2022 for the project, Lian told Wan Shaharuddin that he had still paid the RM1 million before receiving any government payments “because we calculated, that project has profits”.
While confirming that the project’s award could be cancelled at any time if Nepturis breaches the contract’s conditions, Lian said he had still paid the RM1 million as he already had an understanding with Azman that the payment had to be made once the company gets the contract.
As of today, Lian said Nepturis had completed 98 per cent of the project and that it is almost done.
Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad, who was known as Segambut Bersatu deputy chief, is seen here at the Kuala Lumpur court complex on February 16, 2024. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
About Azman and Adam Radlan
Earlier, Lian said he does not personally know Muhyiddin, and only knew of the latter as a politician.
Lian said he had met with Azman in the latter’s car at Bank Rakyat in Kuala Lumpur in 2020 to ask about government project opportunities for Nepturis, insisting today that the company still has Bumiputera status as his two Bumiputera employees’ 70 per cent ownership exceeds the 51 per cent Bumiputera ownership requirement.
Lian said Azman told him of the government’s Jana Wibawa programme for Bumiputera contractors, and that companies who wish to get projects under Jana Wibawa need to get then-PM Muhyiddin’s support.
Lian said Azman also told him that Adam Radlan is Muhyiddin’s close friend and could help in getting Jana Wibawa projects, adding: “Datuk Azman also told me Adam Radlan frequently plays golf with Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and it’s from here that I was confident Adam Radlan could help me to get projects under Jana Wibawa programme.”
After being introduced to Adam Radlan through a meeting arranged by Azman at Publika in December 2020, Lian said Adam Radlan told him of the IPD Klang Utara project and asked him to prepare an application letter in order to get a written minutes of support from Muhyiddin.
Lian said Nepturis director Aliza Abd Malek then prepared five application letters for the same project for Nepturis and four other companies’ names which were “borrowed” with their owners’ knowledge, including Azman’s company Fastcoll Corporation Sdn Bhd.
Lian said he had given these five letters in an envelope to Adam Radlan in a Publika restaurant for him to pass to Muhyiddin.
Lian claimed that Adam Radlan had several days later said Muhyiddin had gave his written minutes of support for Lian’s application letter, but Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad objected to this and said it was hearsay.
After informing Azman of what Adam Radlan said, Lian said Azman had asked him to donate RM1 million directly to Bersatu if Nepturis gets the project as Adam Radlan had asked for then-PM and Bersatu president Muhyiddin’s support, and that he had agreed to Azman’s request.
Lian said he had later informed both Adam Radlan and Azman that Nepturis was awarded the contract, and that Azman had once again asked him to pay RM1 million into Bersatu’s account directly as previously agreed.
After directing Nepturis managing director Mohd Rizman Akum Khan to issue the RM1 million cheque on February 16, 2022, Lian said he had on the same day passed the cheque to Azman at the latter’s office for him to hand it to any Bersatu leader or to deposit it.
Among other things, Lian said he had agreed with Azman’s suggestion to appoint the latter’s company KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd for advice given for the project, saying that he lacked experience for the project which was complicated as it involved technical and safety aspects while Azman was experienced in government tenders.
Lian said Nepturis in a February 23, 2021 letter appointed KCJ as a business development consultant for six months from March 1, 2021, with a consultant fee of RM1 million which was paid to KCJ in stages (RM300,000 through an online bank transfer, and seven cheques of RM100,000).
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin continues tomorrow.
In this trial, Muhyiddin faces seven charges — four counts of allegedly abusing his position to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for Bersatu (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Azman Yusoff, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of money laundering involving funds Bersatu allegedly received from Bukhary Equity.
